question: Which path should own the remaining native Linux companion app now that Windows Hub is shipped through current release assets?
rationale: The observable gap is no longer a simple Linux/Windows missing-app pair: Windows has a shipped path, while Linux has competing broad GTK/C and Rust/GTK4 implementation candidates with security, packaging, and ownership tradeoffs that automation should not choose.

options.title: Split and select a Linux track
options.body: Keep this as the umbrella only long enough to pick the Linux architecture, then move implementation into narrower reviewable Linux milestones and close or retitle the Windows portion as shipped.

options.title: Adopt the GTK/C candidate
options.body: Sponsor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/59859 as the canonical Linux path and require focused security, packaging, and real desktop proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Linux gateway-only for now
options.body: Defer native Linux app work and document Windows Hub plus Linux Gateway support as the current platform boundary until maintainers explicitly resume desktop app investment.

recommendation.title: Split and select a Linux track
recommendation.body: Keep this as the umbrella only long enough to pick the Linux architecture, then move implementation into narrower reviewable Linux milestones and close or retitle the Windows portion as shipped.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and current platform-status docs show steipete shaping the product direction and review boundary for this tracker.
